facts.text: Saint Paul was named the capital of the Minnesota Territory in 1849, cementing its role as a center of commerce, government, and culture.
The city’s defining feature is the confluence of the Mississippi and Minnesota Rivers, a landscape carved by the last ice age into steep bluffs and dramatic palisades.
Saint Paul’s historic Landmark Center downtown hosts a cluster of cultural and arts organizations that have shaped the city’s creative scene for decades.
The first wave of Irish immigrants settled at Connemara Patch along the Mississippi, naming the neighborhood after their homeland in Ireland.
The city’s railroad history began with Hill, who founded a transcontinental empire that helped make Saint Paul a key transportation hub.
Saint Paul’s strategic riverside location made it a long‑standing trade hub, a fact highlighted by its early role as a military reservation at the river confluence.
